SECTION 2: TERMS, DEFINITIONS & PURPOSE
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

IP ADDRESS (Internet Protocol Address)
  The "street address" of a device on a network. Every device needs one to
  send and receive data. Like a house number in a street. Your PC is number
  19. The router is number 1. CO is number 5. HO is number 6.

MAC ADDRESS (Media Access Control Address)
  The "serial number" of a network card. Permanently burned into the hardware
  at the factory. Unchangeable. Used by the router to know which physical
  device is which, even if the IP address changes. Format: XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX
  First 3 pairs identify the manufacturer (e.g. Intel = e8:f4:08).

GATEWAY (Default Gateway)
  The "front door" of your network. All traffic leaving your house goes
  through the gateway (192.168.20.1). If the gateway is down, no internet.
  Your gateway is the NetComm NF10WV modem/router provided by Dodo.

SUBNET MASK
  Defines how many devices can exist on your network. 255.255.255.0 means
  254 possible devices (256 minus the gateway and broadcast address). Your
  network can support 254 devices before needing expansion.

DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol)
  The "reception desk" of the router. When a new device connects to Wi-Fi,
  DHCP assigns it an available IP address automatically. Without DHCP, you'd
  manually configure every device. Your lease lasts ~13 days before renewal.

DNS (Domain Name System)
  The "phone book" of the internet. When you type "vistamations.com," DNS
  translates that to a numeric IP address that computers understand. Your
  router (192.168.20.1) handles local DNS; Google's 8.8.8.8 handles external.

ARP (Address Resolution Protocol)
  The router's "neighbour list." Every device on the network broadcasts its
  IP and MAC address periodically. The router maintains this table so it
  knows where to send data. Your ARP table shows 7 active neighbours.

ISP (Internet Service Provider)
  Dodo. The company that provides your internet connection. Your router
  connects to Dodo's infrastructure via FTTN/VDSL (Fibre to the Node +
  copper to your house). Dodo assigns your public IP address.

WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)
  A virtual machine running inside Windows. Creates a second network
  (172.26.128.0/20) that Docker uses. Visible as the Hyper-V Virtual
  Ethernet Adapter. Docker containers run inside this virtual network.

NODE TYPE: HYBRID
  Your PC uses both broadcast name resolution (NetBIOS) and DNS for
  finding other computers. Hybrid = tries DNS first, then broadcasts if DNS
  fails. The most reliable configuration for mixed-device networks.

Lease
  The time period a DHCP-assigned IP address is valid. Your current lease
  started 31-Jul-2026 and expires 13-Aug-2026. When it expires, the router
  may assign a new IP address unless the device requests renewal.

4.3 SUITABLE FILE FORMATS FOR NETWORK RECORDS

  | Format | Best for | Notes |
  |--------|----------|-------|
  | JSON | Machine-readable inventory | Already built (see 4.1) |
  | TXT | Human-readable documentation | This file (network-map.txt) |
  | CSV | Spreadsheet import | Devices table exportable |
  | YAML | Configuration management | Docker-compose style |
  | Mermaid | Topology diagrams | Network graph rendering |
  | SVG/PNG | Infographics | Visual map (see homeplug folder) |
